title: The tank's volume from its level transmitter
statement: An S7-300 reads a horizontal cylindrical tank's level transmitter at PIW 256 and works out the volume, network by network, in the STL listing below. For each raw value, fill in the corrected value in MW 20, the level $h$, the wetted area $A$ and the volume $V$.
given: raw $0$ to $27648$ is empty to full

artefact.caption: Each network in turn, three raw values

steps.title: Correct the zero point
steps.note: Network 1 adds the offset with $+I$: $13624 + 200 = 13824$. An INT sum past $32767$ would wrap and set OV, which latches M 1.2.

steps.title: Scale with FC105
steps.note: FC105 maps $0$ to $27648$ onto $0$ to $2.0\ \text{m}$: $h = \frac{13824}{27648} \cdot 2.0 = 1.0\ \text{m}$, and RET_VAL stays $0$ inside the range.

steps.title: The wetted area
steps.note: Network 3 works out $A = r^2 \arccos\frac{d}{r} - d \sqrt{2rh - h^2}$ with $d = r - h$. Half full, $d = 0$ and $A = \frac{\pi r^2}{2} = 1.5708\ \text{m}^2$.

steps.title: The volume
steps.note: Network 4 multiplies by the length and by $1000$: $V = 1.5708 \cdot 4.0 \cdot 1000 = 6283.2$ litres. Every step is a REAL, so the PLC holds $6283.1855$.

answer: At the raw value $13624$ the tank is half full: MW 20 holds $13824$, $h = 1.0\ \text{m}$, $A = 1.5708\ \text{m}^2$ and $V = 6283.2$ litres.
